criteria.evidence: Probe at 2599ce39 in a scratch worktree used the round-2 analyser JD '- Experience presenting quarterly results to the board for 3+ years' (keywords [presenting, quarterly, results]) with an A_FEW_TIMES answer. For the details 'Yes, a few times', 'n/a' and 'Yes', AnswerFacts.keywords is []. The fact is only the detail text. Summary 'Presenting quarterly results.' citing ans-<req> gets UnsupportedTerm(Presenting, quarterly, results) and falls back. Skills [SQL, Quarterly, Results] keep [SQL] and remove Quarterly and Results with violations. At edd587d4 the same probe kept all three with no violation. Detail 'Presented quarterly results to the CFO' still yields [presenting, quarterly, results], which D39 allows because the detail states them. The prototype answer on 'Experience presenting to senior stakeholders' with a placeholder detail now gives [] (was [presenting, senior, stakeholders]). AnswerFacts.kt:21-22 matches D39/D41.

Without a source naming the skill, each of these falls back to the profile summary with UnsupportedTerm of the skill: 'Built dashboards with R.', 'Shipped services in C++.', the exact round-2 triggers ('...monthly finance reports with R.' citing b1, '...transaction data and C++.' citing b2), '..., C#.', '... in C.', '...; R.', '..., and Go.' and '...with Express.'. At edd587d4, R, C++, C# and '; R' all passed with violations=[]. Each passes when cited to an answer whose detail states R, C++ or C#. These honest summaries pass with violations=[]: one-fact b1, one-fact b2, the two-clause one-entry sentence, the 'I built ...' sentence, and the prototype two-sentence summary with the CFO answer. 'Built a set of Power BI dashboards...' is flagged UnsupportedTerm(set) identically at edd587d4 (pre-existing guard behaviour; it fails safe). Adding 'a'/'i' to FUNCTION_WORDS only drops clauses that were already dropped by the old length>1 rule (TailorResumeUseCase.kt:122-126, :165).

AnswerFacts.keywords was compared at edd587d4 and 2599ce39 on 21 crafted requirements, the Northwind prototype JD (8 analysed requirements x 3 details) and the 5 resource JDs x {blank, requirement-text} details with sampleProfile. Only one keyword is added, and it is D41-intended: TOOL 'Experience with Express' gives [Express] from the named path, because 'with Express' satisfies requiredPrefix. The AmEx detail adds nothing: a detail-only 'Go through reports at American Express' gives []. 'Go through monthly reports' (SKILL), 'Go above and beyond' (SKILL, was [Go]), 'Experience at American Express' (EXPERIENCE/TOOL), 'R&D exposure' (was [R]) and 'C++ development' (C dropped) all no longer admit. D41 'presenting to senior stakeholders' drops Forecasting. 'angular js' -> [Angular] is unchanged from edd587d4 and tracked as #311. Prototype fixtures: the Northwind requirements give the same answer keywords except the placeholder case above. Every prototype skill is in profile.skills, so the allowlist cannot drop one. The offline tailor proposes no summary or skills (null), so the allowlist is exercised only by remote proposals. Under-confirmations outside the fixtures are in the finding.

Head TailorResumeUseCaseTest copied onto edd587d4: placeholderDetailAddsNoRequirementKeywords, detailKeywordsAreOnlyThoseTheDetailStates and oneLetterSkillClausesAreCheckedAgainstSources FAIL. honestOneFactSummariesStillPass passes there; it is a regression guard. :core:domain:testDebugUnitTest at 2599ce39 runs 664 tests with 0 failures. The lexicon files and KeywordsStatedInTest are byte-identical to #309 b41ab2c9 (git diff --quiet on all six).

At 2599ce39 these pass: Static checks, Core unit tests, App unit tests, Feature unit tests, Lint, Screenshot tests, Constitution policy, Build/lint/unit, and delivery-gates-pregate. Assemble APKs was still pending when this review was written. mergeStateStatus is CLEAN.

findings.rule: D46 (a precision gap that only under-confirms becomes a follow-up issue), D41
findings.trigger: The #309 strict check now runs on the requirement text in isNamedSkillKeyword. It treats inflected loose aliases as not stating the skill, so a truthful YES no longer admits the named skill to the #308 skills allowlist. The probe compared edd587d4 with 2599ce39 on the resource JDs with a blank detail. 'Experience with REST APIs and Git' goes from [REST API, Git] to [Git] ('rest apis' is a loose alias of REST API, TechLexicon.kt:80). 'Write unit tests with JUnit...' goes from [Unit Testing, JUnit] to [JUnit] ('unit tests', TechLexicon.kt:107). 'Must be detail oriented...' loses Attention to Detail. 'MBA or equivalent postgraduate degree' loses Master's Degree. A remote-proposed skills line with 'REST API' is now trimmed with UnsupportedTerm unless the profile lists it. There is no truth risk and the prototype fixtures are not affected.
findings.title: Plural or inflected loose aliases ('REST APIs', 'unit tests') no longer confirm the named skill the user answered YES to
findings.proof: Under D46, file a follow-up and do not block #308. Fix there: in SkillLexicon.isLooseAlias, treat the surface as strict when keyOf(surface).trimEnd('s') equals keyOf(display).trimEnd('s'), reusing surfaceMatchesDisplay, or move plural forms such as 'rest apis' from loose to aliases. Test: AnswerFacts.keywords(YES, req('Experience with REST APIs and Git', SKILL, 'rest api', 'git')) contains 'REST API'.
